scenario.description: Inspect the example as written: compare non-nested parameter selection with nested outer-fold evaluation across repeated Iris trials.

facts.claim: The example's stated purpose is to compare non-nested and nested cross-validation on Iris.

anchors.quote:
This example compares non-nested and nested cross-validation strategies on a
classifier of the iris data set. Nested cross-validation (CV) is often used to
train a model in which hyperparameters also need to be optimized. Nested CV
estimates the generalization error of the underlying model and its
(hyper)parameter search. Choosing the parameters that maximize non-nested CV
biases the model to the dataset, yielding an overly-optimistic score.

facts.claim: The source explains that inner GridSearchCV selects hyperparameters while outer cross_val_score estimates generalization over held-out folds.

anchors.quote:
To avoid this problem, nested CV effectively uses a series of
train/validation/test set splits. In the inner loop (here executed by
:class:`GridSearchCV <sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV>`), the score is
approximately maximized by fitting a model to each training set, and then
directly maximized in selecting (hyper)parameters over the validation set. In
the outer loop (here in :func:`cross_val_score
<sklearn.model_selection.cross_val_score>`), generalization error is estimated
by averaging test set scores over several dataset splits.

facts.claim: Features and labels come from sklearn's Iris dataset loader.

anchors.quote:
# Load the dataset
iris = load_iris()
X_iris = iris.data
y_iris = iris.target

facts.claim: Grid search considers C values 1, 10, and 100 and gamma values 0.01 and 0.1.

anchors.quote:
# Set up possible values of parameters to optimize over
p_grid = {"C": [1, 10, 100], "gamma": [0.01, 0.1]}

facts.claim: The estimator is an SVC with an RBF kernel.

anchors.quote:
# We will use a Support Vector Classifier with "rbf" kernel
svm = SVC(kernel="rbf")

facts.claim: Each trial constructs separate shuffled four-fold inner and outer KFold objects, both seeded by the trial index.

anchors.quote:
# Loop for each trial
for i in range(NUM_TRIALS):
    # Choose cross-validation techniques for the inner and outer loops,
    # independently of the dataset.
    # E.g "GroupKFold", "LeaveOneOut", "LeaveOneGroupOut", etc.
    inner_cv = KFold(n_splits=4, shuffle=True, random_state=i)
    outer_cv = KFold(n_splits=4, shuffle=True, random_state=i)

facts.claim: The non-nested score is GridSearchCV.best_score_ after fitting the search over the full Iris inputs with outer_cv as its CV splitter.

anchors.quote:
# Non_nested parameter search and scoring
    clf = GridSearchCV(estimator=svm, param_grid=p_grid, cv=outer_cv)
    clf.fit(X_iris, y_iris)
    non_nested_scores[i] = clf.best_score_

facts.claim: The nested score wraps the inner GridSearchCV in cross_val_score using outer_cv, then averages the outer scores.

anchors.quote:
# Nested CV with parameter optimization
    clf = GridSearchCV(estimator=svm, param_grid=p_grid, cv=inner_cv)
    nested_score = cross_val_score(clf, X=X_iris, y=y_iris, cv=outer_cv)
    nested_scores[i] = nested_score.mean()

facts.claim: The reported comparison is non-nested score minus nested score, summarized by mean and standard deviation.
The visualization shows both score sequences and a bar chart of their per-trial difference.

anchors.quote:
# Plot scores on each trial for nested and non-nested CV
plt.figure()
plt.subplot(211)
(non_nested_scores_line,) = plt.plot(non_nested_scores, color="r")
(nested_line,) = plt.plot(nested_scores, color="b")

unknowns: No target code was executed, so numerical score differences and plot contents are not candidate facts.
The implementation details of GridSearchCV, KFold, cross_val_score, and SVC are outside this inspected example.
A human reviewer must decide whether to label non-nested selection bias as a demonstrated methodological pitfall rather than a defect in this educational example.
nonDefects: The non-nested reuse of CV for selection and scoring is intentional because the example demonstrates its optimistic bias.
Using the same trial index to seed separate inner and outer splitter objects is explicit example behavior and is not, by itself, evidence of leakage.
The script compares evaluation strategies; it does not produce a final deployed estimator.
